A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CONTRABIN research. All 12 pages of v2 and 15 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, and end matter, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF includes an appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification, function-name recovery, summarization, reverse-engineering, embedding, and ablation results in Section 4, Tables 3–7, and Figures 6–8.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds comment-source experiments, a pretraining-objective comparison, a negative case study, and T5/CodeT5 results in Section 5.

M1.justification: Section 5.5 adds an evaluated CONTRABIN(CodeT5) variant, described as adapting the RoBERTa implementation to an encoder-decoder architecture with corresponding tokenization and output/loss adjustments. The original contrastive-learning stages, simplex interpolation, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 5.2 newly uses human-written comments for pretraining alongside the generated comments selected in v2, extending the training data's comment-source coverage. The existing code corpora and four downstream tasks remain; the new architecture comparison also uses POJ104.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds actual comparisons against T5 and CodeT5, and Figure 10 compares a classification case with CodeT5. CodeT5 previously served as a comment generator and related model, rather than an evaluated downstream comparator. The comparator sets in Tables 3–6 are retained.

E3.justification: The original Section 3 protocols and dataset splits are unchanged. Added experiments test simultaneous averaged-loss pretraining and a CodeT5 adaptation whose training duration is reported as 40% of previous rounds. These are additional experimental conditions, not revisions establishing that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends the diagnostic evidence beyond the retained component-removal ablations. Sections 5.2–5.5 test human versus generated comments, staged versus averaged-loss pretraining, a classification failure, and transfer to another architecture. Figure 9 adds comment-length analysis; Figure 10 adds the negative case.

E5.justification: Both versions use fixed seeds, including 42 for pretraining and 123456 for classification fine-tuning. The added CodeT5 experiment follows the existing seed-42 practice. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 3–7 retain their values, but v3 adds substantial auxiliary results. Table 8 reports MAP/MAR/MAF1 of 30.1/22.16/25.53 for CONTRABIN(CodeT5), versus 28.82/21.71/24.76 for CodeT5 and 23.35/17.34/19.90 for T5. Sections 5.2–5.4 add reported human-comment reductions of 40.67%/30.86%/35.13%, reductions exceeding 97% with averaged losses, and a misclassification case. These are newly reported conditions, not same-setting changes to the original scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the formal projection, similarity, and interpolation definitions are retained. The additional loss and manifold discussion is explanatory; no new theorem, proof, derivation, or revised formal assumption is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same three-component framework, multimodal novelty claim, and claimed effectiveness across four downstream tasks. The additional experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations connecting comment consistency to training effectiveness, averaged-loss failure to competing objectives, and the CodeT5 results to architectural portability. Section 5.4 newly discusses a failure of the full model when structural alignment matters, hypothesizing bias from source/comment semantics. It also adds qualifications describing manifold modeling and embedding visualization as conceptual or qualitative.

D1.justification: Figure 2 and Section 2.1 make pretrained encoder initialization explicit. Section 5.5 additionally documents eight Nvidia A100 GPUs for the CodeT5 variant and outlines architecture, tokenization, attention, and output-processing adaptations. Existing implementation settings and access information remain.

R1.justification: The related-work section and 52-entry bibliography are unchanged, but Section 5.5 adds limited positioning around extending CONTRABIN from RoBERTa to T5/CodeT5. T5 is newly discussed with an unresolved citation marker.

P1.justification: V3 expands the background, loss, and embedding explanations and creates a standalone Section 5 containing the former Section 4.5 ablations and new analyses. It also changes author ordering and some headings. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds the comment-distribution plot, negative-case diagram, and architecture-comparison table as Figures 9–10 and Table 8. Figure 2 gains an initialization note, and Figures 7–8 are labeled positive cases. Existing displays are retained with relocation within the same two-column layout.

improvement.justification: V3 improves transparency and evidential support through explicit pretrained initialization, additional tests of comment and training choices, a CodeT5 comparison, and a disclosed failure case. The gain is limited: the original benchmark evidence is unchanged, Sections 5.2–5.3 report performance losses only as percentages without absolute scores or uncertainty, and the negative case does not establish overfitting as its cause.
